paragraphs: National Health Investors, Inc. ("NHI", the "Company", "we", "us" or "our"), established in 1991 as a Maryland corporation, is a self-managed real estate investment trust ("REIT"). We own, lease, operate and finance the development of high-quality real estate properties, focusing on senior housing communities and medical facilities. We operate through two reportable segments, Real Estate Investments and Senior Housing Operating Portfolio ("SHOP").

Our investments in senior housing communities, also referred to as senior housing properties ("SHO"), include independent living facilities ("ILF"), assisted living facilities ("ALF"), entrance fee communities ("EFC") and senior living campuses ("SLC"). Our investments in medical facilities include skilled nursing facilities ("SNF") and hospitals ("HOSP"). Our financing arrangements consist of mortgages, construction loans, mezzanine loans and revolving lines of credit extended to our tenants, operators, or affiliates of our tenants and operators, and other third parties.

As of December 31, 2025, our Real Estate Investments segment consisted of gross real estate investments of $2.7 billion in 176 properties, excluding one property classified as assets held for sale, which are located in 32 states and leased pursuant primarily to triple-net leases to 31 tenants. These investments included 110 SHOs, 65 SNFs and one HOSP. Additionally, our investments included $218.7 million in principal amounts of mortgage and other notes receivable, excluding $15.4 million of credit loss reserves.

As of December 31, 2025, our SHOP segment consisted of gross real estate investments of $634.3 million in 26 senior housing communities located in 13 states and comprised of 17 ILFs, six SLCs and three ALFs with a combined total of 3,009 units. We outsource the operations at these properties to third-party managers and pay a management fee for these services. As of December 31, 2025, 16 of our senior housing communities were held in consolidated partnerships in which the noncontrolling common equity interests are owned by affiliates of the respective managers.

In our Real Estate Investments segment, our revenues primarily relate to triple-net leases with third-party operators at our properties. Additionally, we recognize interest income from financing arrangements we provide to our tenants, operators, or affiliates of our tenants and operators, and other third parties primarily for construction, renovation and expansion projects, funding of working capital or corporate needs and the acquisition of real estate properties. Our SHOP segment is comprised of senior housing communities from which we generate revenues from resident fees and services on each unit. We utilize third-party managers to operate these properties on our behalf and pay a management fee for their services.

We fund our real estate investments primarily through: (1) operating cash flows, (2) debt offerings, including revolving lines of credit and term debt that are both unsecured and secured, and (3) sales of equity securities. Our investments in real estate and the real estate properties that secure our mortgage loans are located within the United States. Information about our revenues from tenant leases, resident fees and services, and loans and information on our financial condition, results of operations and cash flows can be found in "Part II, Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data" of this Annual Report.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, our total revenues were $375.6 million, an increase of 12.1% over the prior year, consisting of $271.6 million of rental income, $80.1 million of resident fees and services and $24.0 million of interest and other income. Rental income, resident fees and services and interest and other income represented 72.3%, 21.3% and 6.4%, respectively, of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025. Our revenues depend on the operating success of our tenants, managers and borrowers whose sources and amounts of revenues are determined by factors including, but not limited to (i) the number of licensed beds or units at each facility, (ii) occupancy rates, (iii) the extent to which services are utilized by the residents and patients, (iv) the mix of private pay, Medicare and Medicaid patients and (v) the rates paid by private health insurance, Medicare and Medicaid programs.

As of December 31, 2025, our investments comprising the Real Estate Investments segment included real estate properties and financing arrangements involving 189 properties located in 32 states, excluding one property classified as assets held for sale. The aggregate gross carrying value of the owned properties was $2.7 billion, which included 110 SHOs, 65 SNFs and one HOSP leased to 31 tenants. The aggregate gross carrying value of our mortgage and other notes receivable was $218.7 million, excluding $15.4 million of credit loss reserves.

As of December 31, 2025, our investments included in the SHOP segment consisted of 17 ILFs, six SLCs and three ALFs located in 13 states with a combined total of 3,009 units. The aggregate gross carrying value of these properties was $634.3 million. We have structured the operations at these senior housing communities to comply with the requirements of the REIT Investment Diversification and Empowerment Act of 2007 ("RIDEA") and to utilize our taxable REIT subsidiaries ("TRS") for activities that would otherwise be non-qualifying for REIT purposes.

We classify our investments in real estate properties as either SHOs or medical facilities and further classify our SHOs as either need-driven or discretionary properties based on the differing credit risk profiles represented by the underlying revenue sources.
A summary of information related to these classifications follows: Need-Driven Senior Housing

Assisted Living Facilities - As of December 31, 2025, our Real Estate Investments segment included 86 ALFs leased to third-party operators and six ALFs secured by mortgage loans with us. In our SHOP segment, we had three ALFs as of December 31, 2025 which are operated by third-party managers on our behalf. ALFs are free-standing facilities that provide basic room and board functions for elderly residents. As residents typically receive assistance with activities of daily living, such as bathing, grooming, administering medication and memory care services, we consider these facilities to be need-driven senior housing. On-site staff personnel at these facilities are available to assist with minor medical needs on an as-needed basis. Operators of ALFs are typically paid from private payor sources without government assistance through the Medicare and Medicaid programs. ALFs may be licensed and regulated in some states, but generally do not require the issuance of a Certificate of Need ("CON") as is often required for SNFs.

Senior Living Campuses - As of December 31, 2025, our Real Estate Investments segment included nine SLCs leased to third-party operators and two SLCs secured by mortgage loans with us. In our SHOP segment, we had six SLCs as of December 31, 2025 which are operated by third-party managers on our behalf. SLCs generally have one or more buildings and typically include a higher acuity level of care for residents. For example, an SLC may offer skilled nursing beds in combination with independent or assisted living accommodations providing basic room and board functions to elderly residents. They may also provide assistance to residents with activities of daily living, such as bathing, grooming, administering medication and memory care services. On-site staff personnel are available to assist with minor medical needs on an as-needed basis. As the decision to transition to a SLC is typically more than a lifestyle choice and is usually driven by a resident's need for some moderate level of care, we consider these types of SHOs to be need-driven. Operators of SLCs are typically paid through private payor sources and when skilled nursing care is involved, they may also be paid from government assistance programs, including Medicare and Medicaid. SLCs may be licensed and regulated as nursing homes in some states and may also require a CON.

Independent Living Facilities - As of December 31, 2025, our Real Estate Investments segment included three ILFs leased to third-party operators and one ILF secured by a mortgage loan with us. In our SHOP segment, we had 17 ILFs as of December 31, 2025 which are operated by third-party managers on our behalf. ILFs offer specially designed residential units for active senior adults and provide various ancillary services for their residents including restaurants, activity rooms and social areas. Services provided by ILF operators are generally paid from private payor sources without government assistance through the Medicare and Medicaid programs. ILFs are generally, but not always, unlicensed facilities and do not require the issuance of a CON as required for SNFs. As ILFs typically do not provide assistance with the activities of daily living, we consider the decision of a senior adult to transition to an ILF to be discretionary.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
We are exposed to the risk that our tenants, managers and borrowers may become subject to bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings.
Actual or perceived risks associated with pandemics, epidemics or outbreaks have had, and may in the future, have a material adverse effect on our operators' business and results of operations.
A member of our Board of Directors is also the chairman of the board of directors of NHC, and his interests may differ from those of our stockholders.
We are exposed to the risk that the cash flows of our tenants, managers and borrowers may be adversely affected by increased liability claims and liability insurance costs.
Significant legal or regulatory proceedings could adversely affect the liquidity, financial condition and results of operations of our tenants, managers and borrowers.
We are exposed to the risk that we may not be fully indemnified by our tenants, managers and borrowers against future litigation.
We depend on the success of property development and construction activities, which may fail to achieve the operating results we expect.
We are exposed to the risk that the illiquidity of real estate investments could impede our ability to respond to adverse changes in the performance of our properties.
Our investments are concentrated in healthcare properties.

We are subject to risks related to our investment with Life Care Services for Timber Ridge, an entrance fee CCRC, associated with Type A benefits offered to the residents of the CCRC and related accounting requirements.
Risks related to our joint venture investments could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Inflation and increased interest rates may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Adverse geopolitical developments could have a material adverse impact on our business.
We are exposed to operational risks with respect to our SHOP structured communities.
We are exposed to risks related to environmental laws and the costs associated with liabilities related to hazardous substances.
We are subject to risks of damage from catastrophic weather and other natural or man-made disasters and the physical effects of climate change.
We depend on the success of our future acquisitions and investments.
We depend on our ability to reinvest cash in real estate investments in a timely manner and on acceptable terms.
Competition for acquisitions may result in increased prices for properties.
We depend on our ability to retain our management team and other personnel and attract suitable replacements should any such personnel leave.
We are exposed to the risk that our assets may be subject to impairment charges.
Stockholder activism efforts could cause us to incur substantial costs, divert management's attention and have an adverse effect on our business.
paragraphs: There are many significant factors that could materially adversely impact our financial condition, results of operations, cash flows, distributions and stock price. The following are risks we believe are material to our stockholders. There may be additional risks and uncertainties that we have not presently identified or have not deemed material. Some of the following risk factors constitute forward-looking statements. Please refer to "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" at the beginning of this Annual Report.

We depend on the operating success of our tenants, managers and borrowers and if their financial condition or business prospects deteriorate, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be adversely affected.

We rely on our tenants, managers and borrowers and their ability to perform their obligations to us under leases, management agreements and loan arrangements. Any of our tenants, managers or borrowers may experience a weakening in their overall financial condition as a result of deteriorating operating performance, changes in industry or market conditions, such as rising or elevated interest rates or inflation, increases in operating and borrowing costs, including labor costs, or other factors. If the financial condition of any of our tenants, managers or borrowers deteriorates, they may be unable or unwilling to make payments or perform their obligations to us in a timely manner, if at all.

Our operators' revenues are also driven by occupancy rates. Periods of weak economic growth in the U.S. that affect housing sales, investment returns and personal incomes, as well as with an oversupply of senior housing real estate, may adversely affect senior housing occupancy rates. In addition, our operators are experiencing increasing cost pressures. Labor and other operating costs have continued to rise, and historically low unemployment levels have contributed to significant wage pressure.

To the extent any decrease in revenues and/or any increase in operating expenses of our operators results in a property not generating enough cash to make scheduled payments to us, our revenues, net income and funds from operations would be adversely affected. Such events and circumstances would cause us to evaluate whether there was an impairment of the real estate or mortgage loan that should be charged to earnings. Such impairment would be measured as the amount by which the carrying amount of the asset exceeded its fair value. Consequently, we might be unable to maintain or increase our current dividends and the market price of our stock may decline.

The insolvency or bankruptcy of our tenants, managers and borrowers may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. Although our lease agreements provide us the right to evict a tenant/operator and demand immediate payment of rent and exercise other remedies, and our mortgage loans provide us the right to terminate any funding obligations, demand immediate repayment of principal and unpaid interest, foreclose on the collateral and exercise other remedies, in the event our counterparty has filed for bankruptcy or reorganization, the bankruptcy laws afford certain rights to a party that has filed for bankruptcy or reorganization. A tenant or borrower in bankruptcy may be able to limit or delay our ability to collect unpaid rent in the case of a lease or to receive unpaid principal and/or interest in the case of a mortgage loan and to exercise other rights and remedies. For example, a tenant may reject its lease with us in a bankruptcy proceeding. In such a case, our claim against the tenant for unpaid and future rents would be limited by the statutory cap of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code. This statutory cap could be substantially less than the remaining rent owed under the lease, and any claim we have for unpaid rent might not be paid in full. In addition, a tenant may assert in a bankruptcy proceeding that its lease should be re-characterized as a financing agreement. If such a claim is successful, our rights and remedies as a lender, compared to a landlord, are generally more limited. We may be required to fund certain expenses, such as real estate taxes, maintenance and capital improvements, to preserve the value of a property, avoid the imposition of liens on a property and/or transition a property to a new tenant or borrower. In some instances, we have terminated our lease with a tenant and leased the facility to another tenant. In certain of those situations, we provided working capital loans to, and limited indemnification of, the new tenant. If we cannot transition a leased facility to a new tenant, we may take possession of that property, which may expose us to certain successor liabilities. Should such events occur, our revenues and operating cash flows may be adversely affected.

paragraphs: National Health Investors, Inc., established in 1991 as a Maryland corporation, is a self-managed REIT. We own, lease, operate and finance the development of high-quality real estate properties, focusing on senior housing communities and medical facilities. We operate through two reportable segments, Real Estate Investments and SHOP. Our investments in senior housing communities, also referred to as SHOs, include ILFs, ALFs, EFCs and SLCs. Our investments in medical facilities include SNFs and HOSPs.

In our Real Estate Investments segment, our revenues primarily relate to triple-net leases with third-party operators at our properties. Additionally, we recognize interest income from financing arrangements we provide to our tenants, operators, or affiliates of our tenants and operators, and other third parties primarily for construction, renovation and expansion projects, funding of working capital or corporate needs and the acquisition of real estate properties. In our SHOP segment, we own and operate senior housing communities and generate revenues from resident fees and services. We utilize third-party managers to operate these properties on our behalf and pay a management fee for their services. Our investments across both segments are funded primarily through (i) operating cash flows, (ii) debt offerings, revolving lines of credit and term loans and (iii) sales of equity securities.

As of December 31, 2025, our investments comprising the Real Estate Investments segment included real estate properties and financing arrangements involving 189 properties located in 32 states, excluding one property classified as assets held for sale. The aggregate gross carrying value of these owned properties was $2.7 billion, which included 110 SHOs, 65 SNFs and one HOSP leased to 31 tenants. The aggregate gross carrying value of our mortgage and other notes receivable was $218.7 million, excluding $15.4 million of credit loss reserves.

Our tenant leases are typically structured as triple-net leases and relate to single-tenant properties having an initial lease term of 10 to 15 years with one or more five-year extension options. Most of our tenant leases contain annual rent escalators, which may be fixed or variable. Lease payments due to us that are subject to a variable rent escalator are typically determined annually and calculated using a variable index, such as the consumer price index ("CPI") or an index that is dependent on a future date and indeterminable at the inception of the lease.

As of December 31, 2025, our investments included in the SHOP segment consisted of 17 ILFs, six SLCs and three ALFs located in 13 states with a combined total of 3,009 units. The aggregate gross carrying value of these properties was $634.3 million. We have structured the operations at these senior housing communities to comply with the requirements of RIDEA and to utilize our TRS for activities that would otherwise be non-qualifying for REIT purposes.

The properties are operated by third-party managers in exchange for a management fee from us, and as such, we are not directly exposed to the credit risk of the managers in the same manner or to the same extent as we are related to our triple-net tenant leases. However, we rely on the managers' personnel, expertise, technical resources and information systems, proprietary information, good faith and judgment to manage our communities efficiently and effectively. We also rely on the managers to set appropriate resident fees and to operate our communities in compliance with the terms of our management agreements and all applicable laws and regulations.
Classifications of Real Estate Properties

We classify our investments in real estate properties as either SHOs or medical facilities and further classify our SHOs as either need-driven or discretionary properties based on the differing credit risk profiles represented by the underlying revenue sources.
A summary of each of these classifications follows: Need-Driven Senior Housing

Need-driven senior housing properties include ALFs and SLCs which primarily attract private payment for services from residents who require assistance with activities of daily living. Need-driven properties are subject to regulatory oversight.

Discretionary senior housing properties include ILFs and EFCs which primarily attract private payment for services from residents who are making the lifestyle choice of living in an age-restricted, multi-family community that offers social programs, meals, housekeeping, and in some cases, access to healthcare services. Discretionary properties are subject to limited regulatory oversight. There is a correlation between demand for this type of community and the strength of the housing market.

paragraphs: National Health Investors, Inc. ("NHI", the "Company", "we", "us" or "our"), 於1991年成立為馬裏蘭州公司，為一自營的不動產投資信託 ("REIT")。本公司擁有、租賃、營運及籌資開發高品質的不動產資產，專注於長照社區及醫療設施。本公司透過兩個應報告分部進行營運，為不動產投資及長照社區營運組合 ("SHOP")。
本公司在長照社區的投資，亦稱為長照社區 ("SHO")，包括獨立生活設施 ("ILF")、輔助生活設施 ("ALF")、入會費社區 ("EFC") 及長照社區 ("SLC")。本公司在醫療設施的投資包括專業護理設施 ("SNF") 及醫院 ("HOSP")。本公司之融資安排包括房貸、建設貸款、階層貸款及對租戶、營運商或租戶及營運商之關係企業及其他第三方所提供的循環信用線。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司不動產投資應報告分部包含總計2.7十億美元的不動產投資，涉及176處不動產，扣除一處被歸類為待售資產，這些不動產位於32州，主要以三重淨租約出租給31家租戶。這些投資包含110處SHOs、65處SNFs及1處HOSP。此外，本公司投資包含218.7百萬美元的房貸及其他應收款本金金額，扣除15.4百萬美元的信用減損備抵。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司SHOP分部之不動產投資總計為634.3百萬美元，共計26處長照社區，位於13個州，包含17處ILF、6處SLC及3處ALF，總計3,009個單位。本公司將這些不動產之營運委外給第三方管理機構，並支付管理費用。截至2025年12月31日，本公司16處長照社區為合併 partnerships 之資產，其中非控制性普通股權益由各管理機構之關係企業所擁有。
在本公司不動產投資分部，本公司之收入主要來自於對第三方營運商之三重淨租賃。此外，本公司亦從對租戶、營運商或租戶及營運商之關係企業及其他第三方所提供之融資安排中確認利息收入，主要為建設、翻修及擴建項目、營運資金或企業需求之資金，以及不動產資產之購入。本公司SHOP分部為長照社區，本公司從每個單位之住民費用及服務中產生收入。本公司委請第三方管理機構代為營運這些不動產，並支付其管理費用。
本公司主要透過以下方式籌資不動產投資：(1) 營運現金流、(2) 債務發行，包括循環信用線及定期債務，皆為無擔保及有擔保之債務，以及(3) 股權證券之發行。本公司之不動產投資及擔保房貸貸款之不動產資產位於美國。有關本公司租賃收入、住民費用及服務收入，以及貸款之資訊，以及本公司財務狀況、營運成果及現金流之資訊，請參閱本年度報告之「第二部分，第8項：財務報表及補充資料」。

截至2025年12月31日，本公司總收入為375.6百萬美元，較前一年成長12.1%，包含271.6百萬美元之租金收入、80.1百萬美元之住民費用及服務收入，以及24.0百萬美元之利息及其他收入。租金收入、住民費用及服務收入以及利息及其他收入分別佔本公司截至2025年12月31日總收入的72.3%、21.3%及6.4%。本公司之收入取決於租戶、管理機構及借款人之營運成效，其收入來源及金額由多種因素決定，包括但不限於：(i) 每個設施之經許可牀位或單位數量、(ii) 佔用率、(iii) 居民及病患使用服務之程度、(iv) 私人支付、醫療保險及醫療補助計畫之病患比例，以及(v) 私人健康保險、醫療保險及醫療補助計畫所支付之費用率。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司投資於應報告分部「不動產投資」的投資項目，包含不動產資產與涉及32州的189處不動產，除外一處被歸類為待售資產。所擁有不動產的總毛賬面價值為2.7十億美元，其中包括110處SHOs、65處SNFs及一所 leased 給31位租戶的HOSP。本公司房貸及其他應收款的總毛賬面價值為218.7百萬美元，除外15.4百萬美元的信貸減損備抵。
截至2025年12月31日，我們在SHOP分部的投資包含17個ILFs、6個SLCs及3個ALFs，位於13個州，總計有3,009個單位。這些不動產的總攬購價值為634.3 百萬美元。我們已針對這些高齡住宅社區的營運結構，以符合2007年《REIT投資分散化與賦權法案》（"RIDEA"）的要求，並利用我們的課稅REIT子公司（"TRS"）進行原本不符合REIT資格的活動。
我們將在不動產的投資歸類為SHOs或醫療設施，並進一步將SHOs歸類為需求驅動型或選擇性設施，根據其背後收入來源所代表的不同信用風險特質。
與這些歸類相關的資訊摘要如下：需求驅動型高齡住宅

輔助生活設施 - 截至2025年12月31日，我們的不動產投資分部包含86個ALFs出租給第三方營運者，以及6個ALFs由我們提供抵押貸款。在SHOP分部，我們截至2025年12月31日有3個ALFs，由第三方營運者代表我們營運。ALFs為獨立設施，為年長居民提供基本的住宿與膳食服務。由於居民通常需要協助處理日常活動，例如洗澡、整理儀容、服藥及記憶照護服務，我們認為這些設施屬於需求驅動型高齡住宅。這些設施的現場工作人員可根據需要協助處理輕微的醫療需求。ALFs的營運者通常從私人支付來源獲取報酬，而不透過Medicare和Medicaid等政府協助計畫。ALFs在某些州可能被許可與監管，但通常不需要發放需要證書（"CON"）如常規護理機構（SNFs）所要求的。

高齡生活校區 - 截至2025年12月31日，我們的不動產投資分部包含9個SLCs出租給第三方營運者，以及2個SLCs由我們提供抵押貸款。在SHOP分部，我們截至2025年12月31日有6個SLCs，由第三方營運者代表我們營運。SLCs通常包含一或多棟建築物，並為居民提供較高階的照護服務。例如，SLC可能提供專業護理牀，同時搭配獨立或輔助生活住宿，為年長居民提供基本住宿與膳食服務。他們也可能協助居民處理日常活動，例如洗澡、整理儀容、服藥及記憶照護服務。現場工作人員可根據需要協助處理輕微的醫療需求。由於轉換至SLC的決定通常不只是生活方式的選擇，而是基於居民對某些中度照護需求的考量，我們認為這類型的SHOs屬於需求驅動型。SLCs的營運者通常從私人支付來源獲取報酬，當涉及專業護理服務時，他們也可能從政府協助計畫，包括Medicare和Medicaid獲取報酬。SLCs在某些州可能被許可為護理之家，也可能需要發放需要證書（"CON"）。

獨立生活設施 - 截至2025年12月31日，我們的不動產投資分部包含3個ILFs出租給第三方營運者，以及1個ILF由我們提供抵押貸款。在SHOP分部，我們截至2025年12月31日有17個ILFs，由第三方營運者代表我們營運。ILFs為主動年長成人提供特別設計的住宅單位，並為居民提供多種輔助服務，包括餐廳、活動室及社交空間。ILF營運者所提供的服務通常從私人支付來源獲取報酬，而不透過Medicare和Medicaid等政府協助計畫。ILFs通常為未經許可的設施，但並非總是如此，且通常不需要發放需要證書（"CON"）如常規護理機構（SNFs）所要求的。由於ILFs通常不提供協助處理日常活動，我們認為年長成人轉換至ILF的決定為選擇性。

paragraphs: National Health Investors, Inc., 於 1991 年成立為馬裏蘭州公司，為一自營 REIT。我們擁有、出租、經營及籌資開發高品質的不動產資產，專注於長照社區及醫療設施。我們透過兩個應報告分部進行營運，為不動產投資及 SHOP。我們在長照社區的投資，亦稱為 SHOs，包括 ILFs、ALFs、EFCs 及 SLCs。我們在醫療設施的投資包括 SNFs 及 HOSPs。

在不動產投資分部，我們的收入主要來自於第三方經營者於我們不動產上的三重淨租賃。此外，我們亦會從為租戶、經營者或租戶及經營者之附屬公司或其他第三方所提供的融資安排中認列利息收入，這些融資主要用於建設、翻修及擴建項目、營運資金或公司需求，以及取得不動產資產。在 SHOP 分部，我們擁有並經營長照社區，並從住民費用及服務中產生收入。我們透過第三方管理機構代為經營這些不動產，並為其服務支付管理費用。我們在兩個分部的投資主要透過 (i) 營運現金流、(ii) 債務發行、循環信用線及定期貸款，以及 (iii) 股權證券的發行來籌資。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司投資組閤中包含應報告分部之不動產投資部分，包含不動產資產與融資安排，涉及位於32州的189處不動產，除外一處被歸類為待售資產。這些自有不動產之總毛攬取價值為2.7十億美元，包含110處SHOs、65處SNFs及一處出租給31位租戶的HOSP。本公司之房貸及其他應收款總毛攬取價值為218.7百萬美元，除外15.4百萬美元之信用減損備抵。
我們的租戶租賃通常為三重淨租賃，與單一租戶不動產相關，初始租賃期限為 10 到 15 年，並有 一個或多個 5 年的延長選擇權。我們大多數租戶租賃包含年度租金調漲，可能是固定或變動。因變動租金調漲而應支付給我們的租金通常每年確定，並以變動指數計算，例如消費者物價指數（"CPI"）或依未來日期而定且在租賃開始時無法確定的指數。
截至2025年12月31日，我們在SHOP應報告分部的投資包含17個ILFs、6個SLCs及3個ALFs，這些設施位於13個州，總計有3,009個單位。這些不動產的總合毛利率攜帶價值為634.3 百萬美元。我們已針對這些高齡長者住宅社區的營運進行結構設計，以符合RIDEA的規範，並利用TRS進行原本不符合REIT條件的活動。
這些不動產由第三方管理機構代為經營，我們支付管理費用，因此我們並未如同在三重淨租賃中對管理機構的信用風險有相同程度或相同幅度的直接暴露。然而，我們依賴管理機構的員工、專業知識、技術資源及資訊系統、專屬資訊、誠信及判斷力，以有效且高效地管理我們的社區。我們也依賴管理機構設定適當的住民費用，並依照管理契約的條款及所有適用的法律及法規來運作我們的社區。
不動產資產的分類
我們將不動產投資分為 SHOs 或醫療設施，並進一步將 SHOs 分為需求驅動型或選擇性資產，根據其背後收入來源所代表的不同信用風險特質。
以下為各類別之摘要：需求驅動型高齡住宅
需求驅動型高齡住宅包含ALFs及SLCs，主要吸引需協助執行日常活動之住民以私人支付方式支付相關服務費用。需求驅動型住宅受監管機構監督。
選擇性高齡住宅包含ILFs及EFCs，主要吸引選擇以高齡住宅為生活方式之住民，這些住民居住於限制年齡之多戶住宅社區，並提供社交活動、餐飲、清潔服務，有時亦提供醫療服務。選擇性住宅受有限度之監管機構監督。此類社區之需求與住宅市場強弱有相關性。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
本公司可能面臨租戶、管理人及借款人可能成為破產或財務困難程序之對象之風險。
與疫情、流行病或爆發相關之實際或被認為之風險，已對本公司營運者之業務及營運結果產生重大影響，並可能在未來繼續產生重大影響。
本公司董事會成員亦為 NHC 之董事長，其利益可能與本公司股東之利益不同。
本公司可能面臨租戶、管理人及借款人之現金流可能因增加之責任聲請及責任保險費用而受到不利影響之風險。
重大法律或法規程序可能對本公司租戶、管理人及借款人之流動性、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
本公司可能面臨本公司可能無法由租戶、管理人及借款人獲得充分賠償之風險。
本公司依賴房地產開發及建設活動之成功，而這些活動可能無法達到本公司所預期之營運結果。
我們面臨的風險為不動產投資的流動性不足可能影響我們對不動產績效惡化情況的應變能力。
我們的投資集中於醫療衛生不動產。
我們面臨與 Life Care Services 合資投資 Timber Ridge 入場費 CCRC 的風險，此 CCRC 提供 Type A 福利給住民，並涉及相關會計要求。
與我們合資投資相關的風險可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
通貨膨脹及利率上升可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
不利的國際政治情勢可能對我們的業務產生重大不利影響。
我們面臨與 SHOP 結構化社區相關的營運風險。
我們面臨與環境法規及與危險物質相關的責任成本的風險。
本公司面臨因重大天氣災害及其他自然或人為災難所致之損壞風險，以及氣候變遷所產生之物理影響。
本公司依賴未來收購與投資之成功。
本公司依賴本公司能及時且在可接受條件下，將現金再投資於不動產投資之能力。
收購競爭可能導致不動產價格上漲。
本公司依賴本公司能留住管理團隊及其他員工，並在任何員工離職時吸引合適之替代人選。
本公司面臨資產可能需提列減損費用之風險。
股東 activism 行動可能導致本公司產生重大成本，分散管理層注意力，並對本公司業務產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 許多重大因素可能會嚴重影響我們的財務狀況、營運結果、現金流、分紅及股票價格。以下為我們認為對股東具重大影響的風險。可能還有其他風險與不確定性，我們尚未識別或認為其具重大影響。部分下列風險因素屬於前瞻性陳述。請參閱本年度報告開頭的「關於前瞻性陳述的警示聲明」。
我們依賴租戶、經理人及借款人的營運成效，若其財務狀況或業務前景惡化，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成不利影響。
我們依賴租戶、經理人及借款人的能力，履行其根據租賃契約、管理契約及貸款安排對我們的義務。我們的租戶、經理人或借款人可能因營運表現惡化、產業或市場條件變動，例如利率或通貨膨脹上升、營運及借款成本增加，包括人工成本，或其他因素，導致其整體財務狀況惡化。若租戶、經理人或借款人的財務狀況惡化，其可能無法或不願按時支付或履行對我們的義務。
我們營運者的收入亦受佔用率影響。美國經濟成長疲軟，影響住宅銷售、投資回報及個人收入，以及長照機構不動產供過於求，可能對長照機構佔用率造成不利影響。此外，我們營運者正面臨日益增加的成本壓力。人工及其他營運成本持續上升，歷史低失業率亦導致薪資壓力顯著。
若任何營運者的收入減少及/或營運費用增加，導致某個不動產無法產生足夠現金以支付我們的定期付款，將對我們的收入、淨利潤及 funds from operations 造成不利影響。此等事件及情況可能導致我們評估是否應將不動產或抵押貸款的減值計入損益。此減值將以資產帳面價值超過公允價值的金額衡量。因此，我們可能無法維持或提高現行分紅，且本公司股票的市場價格可能下跌。

我們租戶、經理人及借款人的破產或財務困難可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。雖然我們的租賃契約提供我們有權驅逐租戶/經理人，並要求立即支付租金及行使其他救濟措施，且我們的抵押貸款提供我們有權終止任何資金義務，要求立即償還本金及未償還利息，並對擔保品進行拍賣及行使其他救濟措施，但若我們的交易對手已提出破產或重整申請，則破產法會給予提出破產或重整申請的當事人某些權利。在租戶或借款人的破產程序中，租戶可能限制或延遲我們收取未付租金的權利，或在抵押貸款的情況下收取未償還本金及/或利息，並行使其他權利與救濟措施。例如，租戶可能在破產程序中拒絕與我們的租賃契約。在這種情況下，我們對租戶未付及未來租金的主張將受到美國破產法規定的上限限制。此上限可能遠低於租賃契約下未付租金的金額，且我們對未付租金的主張可能無法全部償還。此外，租戶可能在破產程序中聲請其租賃契約應重新歸類為融資協議。若此聲請成功，我們作為貸款人的權利與救濟措施，相較於作為出租人的權利，通常會受到更多限制。我們可能需要資助某些費用，例如不動產稅、維護及資本改善，以維持不動產價值、避免不動產設立留置權，或轉讓不動產給新租戶或借款人。在某些情況下，我們已終止與租戶的租賃契約，並將設施出租給其他租戶。在某些情況下，我們已向新租戶提供營運資金貸款，並對其提供有限的賠償。若我們無法將出租的設施轉讓給新租戶，我們可能取得該不動產的所有權，這可能使我們面臨某些繼承責任。若發生此等事件，將對我們的收入及營運現金流造成不利影響。
